column1: # Reference set -- raghavendra_2023_scerevisiae
# Single-organism 10 pg S. cerevisiae libraries from
#   Basapathi Raghavendra J, Zorzano M-P, Kumaresan D, Martin-Torres J.
#   "DNA sequencing at the picogram level to investigate life on Mars and Earth."
# Reads: https://zenodo.org/records/8208597 ("MinION low detectability.zip"),
# fetched by bin/comparison/fetch_raghavendra.sh.
# Covers YSC_R1 / YSC_R2 / YSC_R3, the paper's Table 2 row
# "10 pg of YSC-2 yeast extract".
# WHY THIS EXISTS
# A re-analysis of a prior study's deposited reads under THIS pipeline's
# competitive-mapping assignment, so the prior study can be compared
# like-for-like against our numbers rather than Kraken2-against-PlusPF-8 versus
# minimap2-against-a-known-reference. See docs/comparison.md.
# NO CARRIER
# Raghavendra et al. used no genomic carrier. Methods, "Library preparation":
# "The gDNA for the nanopore library was prepared using nuclease-free water and
# the low concentration of the DNA to be tested was directly pipetted from the
# previously diluted samples" and "The whole amount of DNA ... was diluted in
# 25 ul for library preparation", with SQK-LSK114 at halved reagent volumes on
# an R10.4.1 Flongle. No lambda or other filler DNA appears anywhere in the
# paper. There is therefore no role=carrier row and carrier_dna_ng=0 in the
# samplesheet.
# ACCESSION CHOICE -- Saccharomyces cerevisiae, GCF_000146045.2 (ASSUMPTION)
# Methods, "Test samples": "yeast from Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Type II (YSC-2,
# 51,475, Sigma Aldrich) with an average genomic size of ~ 12 Mb". Sigma YSC-2
# is a dried commercial yeast preparation sold by activity, NOT a strain-defined
# culture-collection deposit: no strain designation is given by the supplier or
# by the paper, and no genome assembly is attributable to it. We therefore use
# the standard S. cerevisiae reference genome
#   GCF_000146045.2  strain S288C, assembly R64, complete, 12,071,326 bp
# and record this as an ASSUMPTION, not a strain identification. 12.07 Mb
# corroborates the paper's stated "~12 Mb". Practical impact is small: the
# competing reference here is a bacterium, so strain-level divergence within
# S. cerevisiae cannot reassign reads between the two organisms; it can only
# slightly change the number of reads that map at all.
# HOMO SAPIENS IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT
# The paper reports human reads in every sample and in the negative controls
# (Table 2: 0-1 human reads here). Human is nevertheless not included as a
# contaminant reference. (1) Cost: references are fetched and indexed once per
# reference set and this study needs four sets, so GRCh38 would be downloaded
# and indexed four times. (2) Direction of the error: adding a competitor to a
# competitive assignment can only move reads AWAY from the target organisms,
# never toward them, so omitting human makes these counts an UPPER BOUND on the
# prior study -- the conservative direction with respect to any advantage we
# claim. Unmapped human reads land in the `unassigned` bin, which
# compute_metrics.py reconciles explicitly. To account for them instead, add:
#   Homo sapiens<TAB>GCF_000001405.40<TAB>contaminant<TAB>0<TAB>GRCh38.p14<TAB>documented cross-contamination
# theoretical_dna_fraction: single-organism library, so 1.0 by construction.
organism
Saccharomyces cerevisiae
